comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Fixed, though the diagnosis in the ticket was off by a layer.

Hook failures were **not** swallowed by the backend: `HookResult` already captured stdout/stderr/exit code, the CLI already printed all of it, and the API already returned `hook_results` in the create response. The information was reaching exactly two places nobody looks - a `console.warn` in browser devtools, and **nothing at all in the server log**. Under a background service that is indistinguishable from silence.

Changes:
- `kan serve` now logs every hook failure with command, exit code and stderr. This is what actually catches the reported incident - reproducing it under a bare launchd PATH now yields: `pattern hook "type-shortcut" failed ... exit code 127, stderr: env: rad: No such file or directory`.
- The web UI shows an error toast instead of a silent `console.warn`; `HookInfo` now carries `stderr` and `exit_code` so the toast can say why.
- `kan doctor` hook checks fixed: they previously only fired for commands starting with `/`, `./` or `~/`, so `.kan/hooks/x.rad` - the form our own board uses and the docs recommend - was skipped entirely. Now resolves relative commands against the project root (matching the hook's working dir), checks the executable bit, resolves bare names via PATH, and flags commands with spaces (hooks take no arguments).
- Documented that hooks inherit the server's environment, in the config docs, the doctor code list, and SKILL.md (which recommends the very Rad hook that broke).

Two further bugs found and fixed while in here:
1. The `hook timed out` message was unreachable - a timed-out hook is SIGKILLed, and a killed process still returns `*exec.ExitError`, so that branch always won and you saw a bare `signal: killed`.
2. **The timeout bounded nothing.** `CommandContext` kills the hook but not its grandchildren, which inherit the output pipes, so `cmd.Run()` blocked until they closed. A 1s timeout took 30s to return - meaning a hook that spawns a lingering child would hang card creation in the web UI for that child's full lifetime. Fixed with `cmd.WaitDelay`; regression-guarded with a wall-clock assertion.

Known limitation, deliberately not papered over: `kan doctor` runs with *your* shell's PATH, so it would have reported all-clear during the original incident. It cannot see a background service's PATH. The logging and the toast are what catch that case.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Review round found a regression I'd introduced, plus sharper messaging. Amended:

- **The WaitDelay fix broke fire-and-forget hooks.** `WaitDelay`'s timer starts when the child *exits*, not only on timeout - so a hook doing `something &` then `exit 0` came back as `ErrWaitDelay` and was reported as **failed** (exit -1), with a false error toast on every card create. Worse than the bug being fixed. Now `ErrWaitDelay` with no cancellation is correctly read as success (the hook exited 0; a lingering child just held the pipes). Regression test added.
- **Doctor flagged every hook on Windows.** `Mode().Perm()` never reports the executable bit for a regular file there, so the check was guarded to Unix.
- **Doctor cried wolf on paths containing spaces.** `/Users/John Doe/bin/hook.sh` execs fine, but was flagged as "command has arguments". Now a space is only suspicious when the path itself doesn't exist and the leading token does.
- Windows-relative paths (`.kan/hooks/x.rad` contains no backslash) were misclassified as bare PATH lookups; forward slashes now count as separators everywhere.
- Messaging: the log said `exit code 127, error: exit status 127` - the same fact twice - and printed the internal `-1` sentinel as if it were a real exit code. Both fixed, and the card ID is now in the log line.
- **The missing inference is now supplied.** Exit 127 only means "not found" if you know the convention, and the leap to "my background service has a different PATH" is the expensive one. Failures whose command can't be found now carry a hint saying exactly that - one definition shared by the server log, the web toast, and the CLI.
- **`kan doctor` no longer gives a bare false all-clear.** It checks against the invoking shell's PATH, so during the original incident it would have said "✓ No issues found". When hooks are configured it now qualifies that, pointing at the background-service PATH difference.
- Doctor messages moved to the project's Message/FixAction convention (no more doubled paths), and API-layer tests now pin the two surfaces that matter: the JSON the browser receives, and the log an operator reads.

Committed as b92b45d.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
When a pattern hook fails to execute, kan says nothing. The card is created, the UI looks normal, and the hook's effect just silently doesn't happen. From the user's side this is indistinguishable from "my hook regex didn't match", so you go debug the wrong thing.

Real case, from chat-notes: a type-shortcut hook (`.kan/hooks/type-shortcut.rad`, `#!/usr/bin/env rad`) worked perfectly from the CLI but never fired for cards made in the web UI. Cause: `kan serve` runs as an always-on launchd/beagle service, whose PATH is the bare `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`. That finds neither `rad` (the hook's interpreter) nor `kan` itself (which the hook shells back into), so the exec failed instantly - and kan swallowed it. I burned a while blaming a stale config cache before finding it.

The hook plumbing is fine (api/context.go does wire up HookService). The gap is purely diagnostics. Suggestions:
- Log hook exec failures, loudly - especially ENOENT / non-zero exit / timeout. Include the command, exit code, and stderr.
- Surface it in the web UI too. A card whose hook blew up should say so, not look successful.
- `kan doctor` already validates hook regex/command fields; it could also check the command is actually executable.
- Consider whether serve should pass a saner PATH to hook children, or at least document that hooks inherit the server's environment - that's a sharp edge when serve is a background service rather than a shell process.

Note: I originally filed this as "serve should hot-reload board config". That turned out not to be the bug - serve picks up config fine. Repointed at the actual defect.
title: Pattern hook failures are silent - surface them
